\begin{aligned}A∖B & =A-B \\  & ={1,3,4,5,7,8,10}-{2,4,6,8,10,12} \\  & ={1,3,5,7}.\end{aligned}

after.problem: Let $A$  be the set of all multiples of $3$ greater than $0$ and let $B$  be the set of all multiples of $6$ greater than $0.$ What is $A-B?$
after.worked_solution:
The multiples of $3$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A={3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $6$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B={6,12,18,24,…}.
$$

Now, $A-B$ is the *difference* of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $A$ but *not* in $B.$

The elements of $A$ that are also in $B$ are $6,12,18,24,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $6$). So, we must remove these elements from $A.$ Therefore, we have

$$

Let S be the set of all multiples of 2 greater than 0 and let T be the set of all multiples of 4 greater than 0. What is T∖S?

a
∅
b
{4,8,12,16,…}
c
{0,2,6,10,14,…}
d
{2,4,10,14,…}
e
{0,4,8,12,16,…}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The multiples of 2 that are greater than 0 are

S={2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…}.

Likewise, multiples of 4 that are greater than 0 are

T={4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,…}.

Now, T∖S is the difference of T and S, which means that we want to find the elements that are in T but not in S.

The elements of T that are also in S are 4,8,12,16, and so on (i.e. multiples of 4). So, we must remove these elements from T. Therefore, we have

T∖S={4,8,12,16,…}−{2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…}=∅.

$$
